topic: I. Introduction to Physics - ii. What is Physics?
corefact: Physics is the fundamental science dedicated to understanding how energy, matter, space, and time interact at every scale of the universe. It provides the core rules that govern everything from subatomic particles to colliding galaxies.
domaininsight: Without physics, technologies like smartphones, MRI scans, and space travel could not exist. Mastering these basic principles allows us to predict how real-world objects behave before we ever build or test them.

topic: I. Introduction to Physics - iii. A Mathematical Toolkit
corefact: Mathematics acts as the precise language of physics, allowing scientists to convert physical observations into measurable formulas and equations. Tools like algebra, unit conversions, and scientific notation are essential for tracking real-world physical changes.
domaininsight: Math transforms random guesses into predictable engineering outcomes. Engineers use this exact toolkit to calculate precise rocket trajectories, ensuring spacecraft safely reach their targets across millions of miles.

topic: II. Mechanics - i. Describing Linear Motion
corefact: Linear motion tracks an object moving along a straight line using position, speed, velocity, and acceleration over time. Velocity measures how fast position changes in a specific direction, while acceleration tracks changes in velocity.
domaininsight: Understanding linear motion is critical for safety design in automotive engineering. Crashes are minimized when engineers accurately model how fast vehicles accelerate and how long they take to come to a complete stop.

topic: II. Mechanics - ii. A Mathematical Model of Motion
corefact: Kinematic equations use mathematical models to connect displacement, initial velocity, final velocity, constant acceleration, and time. These relationships allow us to predict an object's exact future position without needing to observe its entire journey.
domaininsight: Video game developers rely heavily on these equations to simulate realistic movement. When a character jumps or a car speeds up, mathematical motion models make the onscreen physics feel natural.

topic: II. Mechanics - iii. Vector Addition (Trigonometry)
corefact: Vectors represent physical quantities that have both magnitude and direction, such as force or velocity. Trigonometry breaks these vectors into horizontal and vertical components so they can be added together accurately.
domaininsight: Airplane pilots must calculate vector addition constantly during flight. Crosswinds push aircraft sideways, requiring navigational adjustments so the plane's true path reaches the correct runway.

topic: II. Mechanics - iv. Projectile Motion
corefact: Projectile motion occurs when an object is launched into the air and moves along a curved path under the influence of gravity alone. Horizontal velocity remains constant (ignoring air resistance) while vertical velocity accelerates downward.
domaininsight: Athletes in sports like basketball and football intuitively calculate projectile motion every time they throw a ball. In engineering, artillery and water display fountains use these exact parabolic trajectories for precise targeting.

topic: II. Mechanics - v. Newton's Laws - Forces
corefact: Newton's Three Laws explain how forces cause motion: objects stay in motion unless acted on, force equals mass times acceleration ($F = ma$), and every action has an equal and opposite reaction. Forces are pushes or pulls that alter an object's motion.
domaininsight: Rocket propulsion is a direct application of Newton's Third Law. By blasting hot gas downward at high speeds, the rocket experiences an equal force pushing it straight up into space.

topic: II. Mechanics - vi. Forces and Motion in Two Dimensions
corefact: Two-dimensional motion involves analyzing forces acting along perpendicular axes simultaneously, such as friction on an inclined plane. Friction resists motion between surfaces, and its strength depends on the normal force pressing the objects together.
domaininsight: Roller coaster designers utilize two-dimensional force analysis to craft safe yet thrilling bank turns. Balancing gravitational force and normal force prevents cars from slipping or derailing at high speeds.

topic: II. Mechanics - vii. Momentum and its Conservation
corefact: Momentum is the product of an object's mass and velocity ($p = mv$), representing how difficult it is to stop. The Law of Conservation of Momentum states that total momentum remains constant in an isolated system during collisions.
domaininsight: Car safety features like airbags and crumple zones are designed around impulse and momentum. By increasing the time it takes for a crash to stop a passenger, the impact force on the body is drastically reduced.

topic: II. Mechanics - viii. Energy, Work, Power, and Simple Machines
corefact: Work is done when a force causes displacement, transferring energy between forms like kinetic and potential energy. Power measures how fast work is performed, while simple machines trade force for distance to make work easier.
domaininsight: Energy cannot be destroyed, only transformed from potential stored state to kinetic motion. Hydroelectric dams harness this principle by transforming the potential energy of elevated water into electrical power for millions of homes.

topic: II. Mechanics - ix. Circular Motion
corefact: Uniform circular motion occurs when an object moves in a circle at a constant speed while constantly changing direction toward the center. This directional change requires a centripetal force constantly pulling the object inward.
domaininsight: Satellites stay in orbit around Earth because gravity acts as a continuous centripetal force. The satellite effectively falls around the planet at high speed without ever hitting the ground.

topic: II. Mechanics - x. Rotational Mechanics
corefact: Rotational mechanics analyzes objects spinning around an axis using rotational equivalents of force, mass, and velocity: torque, rotational inertia, and angular velocity. Torque measures how effectively a force causes an object to rotate.
domaininsight: Figure skaters control their spin speeds using rotational inertia. By pulling their arms inward, they decrease their moment of inertia, causing their rotational speed to dramatically increase.

topic: II. Mechanics - xi. Universal Gravitation
corefact: Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation states that every mass attracts every other mass with a force proportional to their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them. This universal attraction keeps planets orbiting stars.
domaininsight: Gravitational pull dictates tides on Earth due to the Moon's shifting distance and orientation. Oceanographers rely on gravitational models to predict coastal sea levels and marine navigation conditions.

topic: III. Waves and Light - i. Waves and Energy Transfer
corefact: Waves are disturbances that transfer energy through matter or space without permanently moving the medium itself. Key properties include wavelength, frequency, amplitude, and wave speed.
domaininsight: Seismologists analyze earthquake waves passing through the Earth to map underground rock structures. Understanding wave energy helps engineers build earthquake-resistant skyscrapers.

topic: III. Waves and Light - ii. The Nature of Sound
corefact: Sound is a mechanical longitudinal wave produced by vibrating objects that travel through a medium like air, water, or solids. The pitch of a sound corresponds to its frequency, while volume depends on its amplitude.
domaininsight: Noise-canceling headphones utilize wave interference to block background sounds. Microphones capture external noise and instantly produce an inverted sound wave to cancel it out completely.

topic: III. Waves and Light - iii. The Nature of Light
corefact: Light is an electromagnetic wave that can travel through a vacuum at a constant speed of approximately $3 \times 10^8$ meters per second. It exhibits dual behavior, acting both as continuous waves and discrete energy packets called photons.
domaininsight: Solar panels depend directly on the dual nature of light. Photons striking silicon panels knock electrons free, creating usable electric current to power homes and devices.

topic: III. Waves and Light - iv. Colors in Nature
corefact: The color of visible light is determined by its specific wavelength, ranging from red (longer wavelengths) to violet (shorter wavelengths). Objects appear a specific color because they absorb certain wavelengths and reflect or transmit others.
domaininsight: Prisms and raindrops separate white light into vivid rainbows through dispersion. Digital screens combine just three primary colors—red, green, and blue—at varying intensities to generate every color imaginable.

topic: III. Waves and Light - v. Reflection and Refraction
corefact: Reflection occurs when light bounces off a surface at the same angle it hits, while refraction is the bending of light as it passes into a different medium. Refraction happens because light changes speed when transitioning between materials.
domaininsight: Fiber-optic cables transmit high-speed internet across oceans using total internal reflection. Light pulses bounce along glass fibers without escaping, delivering data around the world at light speed.

topic: III. Waves and Light - vi. Mirrors and Lenses
corefact: Mirrors reflect light to form real or virtual images, while curved lenses refract light to converge or diverge light rays. Concave lenses spread light out, whereas convex lenses focus light rays to a single point.
domaininsight: Eyeglasses and contact lenses correct human vision by adjusting how light focuses onto the retina. Microscopes and deep-space telescopes use combinations of lenses to reveal tiny cells or distant galaxies.

topic: III. Waves and Light - vii. Diffraction and Interference
corefact: Diffraction is the bending of waves around obstacles or through narrow openings, while interference occurs when multiple waves overlap and combine. Constructive interference strengthens wave amplitude, while destructive interference cancels it out.
domaininsight: The shimmering iridescent colors on soap bubbles and peacock feathers are caused by thin-film light interference. Engineers use interference patterns in laser measurement systems to detect microscopic structural flaws.

topic: IV. Current Electricity - i. Electrostatics
corefact: Electrostatics is the study of electric charges at rest and the forces between them as described by Coulomb's Law. Opposite charges attract each other, while like charges exert a repulsive force.
domaininsight: Photocopiers and laser printers rely on electrostatic attraction to function. Charged toner powder sticks to specific static patterns on a drum before being heat-fused onto paper.

topic: IV. Current Electricity - ii. Electric Current
corefact: Electric current is the continuous flow of electric charge through a conductor, driven by potential difference (voltage) and limited by resistance. Ohm's Law states that current equals voltage divided by resistance ($I = V/R$).
domaininsight: Battery technology relies on controlling chemical potential to drive electric current. Managing resistance in microchips allows modern electronics to run faster without overheating.

topic: IV. Current Electricity - iii. Electrical Circuits
corefact: Electrical circuits provide closed conductive loops through which current flows to power devices. Components can be arranged in series (single path) or parallel (multiple branches), altering total current and voltage distribution.
domaininsight: Modern home electrical systems use parallel circuits so each outlet receives full voltage independently. This design ensures that turning off a light in one room doesn't cut power to the rest of the house.

corefact: Spanner Graph builds a unified, scale-out database architecture by deeply integrating graph query interfaces directly into Google Spanner's globally distributed relational engine framework.
domaininsight: Siloing graph analysis and transactional data across decoupled platforms introduces expensive data synchronization pipelines and massive system latency. In Q2 2026, leverage Spanner Graph to run highly complex graph algorithms alongside live, high-throughput transactional relational datasets with zero replication overhead.

corefact: The architecture incorporates native, built-in graph algorithm execution support, enabling teams to perform complex centrality, community detection, and topological path analysis using simple query paradigms.
domaininsight: Extracting massive database structures into external processing toolsets for structural network analysis causes severe memory bottlenecks and slows operational velocity. Execute algorithms natively within the storage cluster layer to optimize performance metrics on multi-billion node graphs instantly.

corefact: Deterministic code profiling via built-in modules like cProfile captures precise function call counts, total execution durations, and cumulative execution graphs with low programmatic overhead.
domaininsight: Blindly troubleshooting high-latency python execution streams often leads developers to optimize trivial code structures. Rely on cProfile in Q2 2026 to systematically identify macro-level bottleneck blocks before applying deep manual code rewrites.

corefact: Line-by-line profilers allow engineers to inspect individual instruction latency, hit rates, and execution time percentages directly inside targeted Python functions via standard decorators.
domaininsight: Macro-level profilers isolate slow functions but fail to pinpoint whether the overhead stems from nested loops, data serialization, or slow IO boundaries. Apply the `line_profiler` extension to drill straight into complex functional runtimes and inspect exact execution costs line-by-line.

corefact: Sampling profilers like py-spy inspect the active Python call stack asynchronously at high frequencies without injecting deterministic hooks into the underlying runtime engine.
domaininsight: Traditional deterministic tools introduce significant execution overhead, making them dangerous or unusable on production workloads. Utilize low-impact sampling profilers to generate live flame graphs and diagnose active production bottlenecks without risking system slowdowns.

corefact: PySpark acts as the Python API for Apache Spark, supporting distributed batch processing, structured streaming, and cluster-scale ML pipelines across hundreds of worker nodes.
domaininsight: Single-machine memory limitations block petabyte-scale data engineering. Resolve this in Q2 2026 by utilizing PySpark to build distributed extract, transform, and load (ETL) pipelines that split processing tasks across clustered server instances.

corefact: Dask provides parallel computing abstractions that mirror pandas, NumPy, and scikit-learn APIs, executing tasks lazily on single machines or distributed clusters.
domaininsight: Rewriting legacy pandas codebases for big data is resource-intensive and error-prone. Drop in Dask to break datasets into optimized task graphs, scaling workloads beyond local memory limits with minimal changes to your existing code infrastructure.

corefact: Polars is a highly optimized, multi-threaded DataFrame library written in Rust that leverages the Apache Arrow columnar memory format and lazy query evaluation.
domaininsight: Traditional single-threaded pandas workflows experience severe performance degradation on multi-gigabyte files. Switch execution targets to Polars to benefit from automatic query optimization, lower memory footprint, and high-speed local data transformations.

corefact: Ray is an open-source distributed computing framework that scales Python workloads via a unified task and actor model, utilizing Ray Data for machine learning ingestion pipelines.
domaininsight: Standard distributed clusters often separate data processing from deep learning model training, creating network bottlenecks. Employ Ray to run streaming, batched data loading natively alongside PyTorch or TensorFlow training states across cluster compute fabrics.

corefact: Vaex handles out-of-core DataFrame analysis on a single machine by using memory-mapping and lazy evaluations to analyze billion-row datasets without memory consumption.
domaininsight: Spreading workloads onto cloud clusters for exploratory data analysis increases infrastructure costs unnecessarily. Use Vaex locally to calculate statistical summaries and string transformations instantly over massive datasets without loading files entirely into RAM.

corefact: Apache Kafka (via kafka-python and confluent-kafka clients) acts as a high-throughput, real-time distributed event streaming platform for unbounded data workloads.
domaininsight: Batch processing pipelines fail to deliver the instant feedback loops needed for live telemetry or real-time feature stores. Implement Kafka producers and consumers to stream high-velocity events directly into real-time analytical services.

corefact: DuckDB functions as an embedded, in-process OLAP database engine that processes vectorized SQL queries directly on Parquet, CSV, and JSON formats without an external server.
domaininsight: Deploying full database warehouses for standalone file analytics introduces immense setup overhead. Point DuckDB at raw local or object-storage data files to execute sub-second analytical queries straight from a localized Python runtime environment.

corefact: Unlike human developers who possess contextual knowledge, AI agents depend entirely on explicit, machine-readable API contracts and schemas to execute tasks.
domaininsight: Ambiguous API structures cause agents to 'hallucinate shapes,' causing production execution blockages. Resolve this in Q2 2026 by enforcing strict request/response validation against OpenAPI specs at the gateway edge to reject non-compliant payloads instantly.

corefact: Enforcing deterministic agent behavior requires explicit state lifecycle modeling, uniform pagination patterns, and mandatory idempotency keys for state-changing operations.
domaininsight: Agent errors amplify quickly, turning non-idempotent conflicts into accidental denial-of-wallet loop attacks. Protect infrastructure by enforcing `Idempotency-Key` headers on side-effects and returning structured RFC 7807 problem details payloads.

corefact: In agentic architectures, OpenAPI specifications and integration protocols like MCP serve as live, runtime executable contracts rather than passive documentation.
domaininsight: Wrapping inconsistent legacy APIs in tool discovery layers only accelerates system failures. Optimize specifications for LLM function-calling by stripping vague properties, utilizing explicit `enum` arrays, and providing detailed parameters.
